(6): sum_{j in S_c} omega_j = 1, where omega_j = (sum_{k in S_q} A_jk) / (sum_{l in S_c} sum_{k in S_q} A_lk), under the standing hypothesis that the denominator is nonzero. The Lean 4 theorem 'eq6_omega_normalized' compiles cleanly: it rewrites the sum of ratios into the ratio of the sums, observes that the summed numerator equals the denominator by alpha-equivalence, and applies div_self. No sorry, no sorryAx.

lean.formal_statement: theorem eq6_omega_normalized {α β : Type*} (S_q : Finset α) (S_c : Finset β) (A : β → α → ℝ) (hden : (∑ l ∈ S_c, ∑ k ∈ S_q, A l k) ≠ 0) : (∑ j ∈ S_c, ((∑ k ∈ S_q, A j k) / (∑ l ∈ S_c, ∑ k ∈ S_q, A l k))) = 1 := by rw [← Finset.sum_div]; rw [show (∑ j ∈ S_c, ∑ k ∈ S_q, A j k) = (∑ l ∈ S_c, ∑ k ∈ S_q, A l k) by rfl]; exact div_self hden

results.route_rationale: The fusion-weights 'sum to 1' assertion is checkable against the softmax-row definitions of Eq. (10).

lean_result.reasoning: The paper asserts the fusion weights lambda_v^t = sum_{i in S_I} A_ti and lambda_c^t = sum_{j in S_c} A_tj are 'positive weights that sum to 1'. Formalised the claim as: for any attention row (a probability vector w over the token set partitioned into image S_I, context S_c, query S_q), lambda_v + lambda_c = 1. This is false. The Lean theorem 'eq10_lam_sum_not_one' exhibits a counterexample satisfying every stated hypothesis: uniform attention over {image, context, query} tokens (each weight 1/3) with S_I = {0}, S_c = {1}, S_q = {2} gives lambda_v + lambda_c = 2/3 != 1. A companion theorem 'eq10_lam_sum_le_one' proves the sharp true bound lambda_v + lambda_c <= 1; equality holds only when the attention mass on query/other tokens is zero, which the paper's own Eq. (6) presupposes is not the case. The definitions therefore do not guarantee the stated sum-to-1 normalisation; the description is internally inconsistent unless an undocumented renormalisation is applied.

For beta = 0.7 the argmax token is always retained (max >= 0.7 * max), so the set is nonempty, and zeroing the complement defines a sub-distribution that is renormalised during decoding. This is the standard APC from contrastive decoding; no error.

findings.evidence: Lean refuted the paper's assertion that the logits-fusion weights sum to 1. As defined in Eq. (10), $\lambda_v^t = \sum_{i \in S_I} A_{ti}$ and $\lambda_c^t = \sum_{j \in S_c} A_{tj}$ are partial sums of the attention row $A_{t\cdot}$, which after softmax (Eq. (4)) is a probability distribution over the image, query AND context tokens. Attention mass on query tokens is excluded from both sums, so $\lambda_v^t + \lambda_c^t = 1 - \lambda_q^t < 1$ whenever the model attends to the query. The formal counterexample (uniform attention over {image, context, query}) gives $\lambda_v + \lambda_c = 2/3 \neq 1$ while satisfying every hypothesis the paper states. The sharp true bound, also proved in Lean, is $\lambda_v^t + \lambda_c^t \le 1$, with equality only when attention on query/other tokens is zero — which the paper's own Eq. (6) presupposes does not hold.
findings.exact_quote: Finally, based on the adaptive weights, the logits fusion at decoding step t is performed by a weighted average: $$p(y_t) \sim \text{softmax}\left( \lambda_v^t \cdot \text{logit}_p + \lambda_c^t \cdot \text{logit}_c \right)$$ ensuring positive weights that sum to 1 to consistently balance parametric and contextual knowledge.

summary: Mathematics of 'Boosting Knowledge Utilization in Multimodal Large Language Models via Adaptive Logits Fusion and Attention Reallocation' (ALFAR) verified. Thirteen self-contained mathematical objects were extracted — all display equations; the paper contains no stated theorems or proofs. Two were routed to formal verification in Lean 4 against Mathlib, run strictly serially against the shared project MATH_VERIFICATION/Paper (reused; the project pre-existed with other papers' proofs, so it was kept, not deleted). Eq. (6) — the query-context relevance normalisation $\sum_j \omega_j = 1$ — was proved by the Lean kernel (PASSED). Eq. (10) — the assertion that the logits-fusion weights $\lambda_v^t, \lambda_c^t$ sum to 1 — was REFUTED: the theorem `eq10_lam_sum_not_one` exhibits a probability vector (uniform attention over image/context/query tokens) satisfying every stated hypothesis with $\lambda_v + \lambda_c = 2/3 \neq 1$, and `eq10_lam_sum_le_one` proves the sharp true bound $\lambda_v^t + \lambda_c^t \le 1$, equality requiring zero attention on query tokens. This is reported as a single minor finding (confidence 0.75): the described definitions do not guarantee the stated normalisation, so the fusion description is internally inconsistent unless an undocumented renormalisation is applied — a description imprecision that does not invalidate the paper's empirical claims. The remaining eleven snippets (cosine similarity, softmax decoding, scaled dot-product attention, attention reallocation, parametric/contextual logits definitions, the fusion formula, Conflict Rate, Performance Drop, and the adaptive plausibility constraint) are standard definitions reviewed informally; none contains an algebraic or logical error. No Lean run FAILED, so no fallback reviews were needed and there is no unsettled claim. Verdict: MINOR_ERRORS — one confident minor finding, no critical errors.
